name: runbook-k8s-rerun-job
description: Re-run a failed Kubernetes Job: why it failed (its pods' logs and events) and whether running it again is safe (idempotent, the cause gone), human approval, a new Job from its spec with k8s_control (it waits for it to finish), then verification.

cluster.description: The inventory cluster (empty: the only one).

reason.description: Why it is safe to run again.

precheck.title: Why it failed
precheck.prompt:
Pre-checks for re-running job {{input.job}} in {{input.namespace}} (cluster {{input.cluster}}; reason: {{input.reason}}). Read-only: k8s_describe job/{{input.job}} (conditions, backoff limit, failed pods), k8s_logs for its pods (selector job-name={{input.job}}, errors: true), k8s_events for it.

Report: why it failed (the error lines), whether the cause is transient (a dependency that was down, a timeout) or will fail again (a bug, bad input, missing config), and whether running it twice is safe (idempotent?). Say plainly if a re-run will not help.

approve.title: Approve the re-run
approve.message:
Re-run job {{input.job}} in {{input.namespace}} (cluster {{input.cluster}}) as a new Job? Reason: {{input.reason}}

{{state.precheck}}

rerun.title: Re-run
rerun.prompt:
A person approved re-running job {{input.job}} in {{input.namespace}} (cluster {{input.cluster}}). Run k8s_control once with action rerun-job, target job/{{input.job}}, namespace {{input.namespace}}, reason "{{input.reason}}", and nothing else.

Report: the tool's output (the new job's name and result).

verify.title: Verify
verify.prompt:
Verify the re-run of job {{input.job}} in {{input.namespace}}.

Why it failed:
{{state.precheck}}

Re-run:
{{state.rerun}}

Read-only: k8s_describe the new job (named in the re-run's output): Complete, succeeded >= its completions, no failed pods; k8s_logs of its pod if it failed. VERIFIED when the new job completed; otherwise FAILED.

Report: the checks.
